people.note: Scenario A. Standing, hi-vis, open field, unobstructed. The baseline detection test -- if this one fails, stop and fix the stack.
Scenario C/G. Dark clothing, prone, under canopy shadow. RGB is weak here; thermal carries the detection.
Seated against a fallen tree, half behind brush.
Standing in a forest clearing -- RGB workable, canopy breaks GNSS.
Seated on debris at the edge of the collapse field.
Scenario F/G. Concrete-dust covered, lying among cold slabs. LOW thermal contrast on purpose: this is where a single-sensor detector quits. NOT buried -- torso and head are exposed.
Scenario H. Inside SAR_Building_RUB_002. Visible ONLY through the collapsed wall opening -- there is no line of sight through the intact walls, for RGB or for thermal.
Inside SAR_Building_URB_003, dark interior. Requires entry via the doorway or the collapsed NE corner.
Scenario I. Multi-person triage point, 4 casualties within 4 m.
Rescue personnel kneeling beside a casualty. Tests person-role reasoning, not just person-or-not.

High on the mountain, on a shoulder above where the risky and safe tracks converge, behind rock. Cold and heavily clothed: LOW contrast against sun-warmed rock. Getting here is the risk-aware routing test -- the short track runs the SAR_Ravine_001 rim, the long one climbs the east side.
Avalanche debris field. PARTIALLY snow-dusted and still exposed. Deliberately NOT buried: a LWIR camera cannot see through a snowpack and this environment will not pretend otherwise.
Scenario E. Beside SAR_Vehicle_Civilian_004, whose engine bay is 62 C. Two warm blobs, one of them a person.
Crosses SAR_Road_MainSupply at ~y=70. This is the dynamic obstacle the robot is expected to detect and yield to.
Slow, frequent stops -- behaves like a walking wounded.
Fast mover, dark clothing.
Along SAR_Track_Forest. Repeated occlusion by trunks.
Urban Street A. Crosses paths with PERSON_022 -> multi-target tracking and ID re-assignment test.
Urban Street C, perpendicular to PERSON_021.
Rescuer circulating in the triage cluster.
Walking the main supply route between base and the open field.
Skirting the collapse field. Slow, uneven ground.
East bank of the river, near the stranded vehicle. LOW contrast: wet clothing, cold air off the water.

Walks the main supply route and turns around, so it approaches the robot head-on for half of every cycle. A closing target with almost no lateral optical flow is the case a forward-facing detector handles worst.
Converges with PERSON_029 near (0, 68). Speeds and dwells differ, so the meeting drifts through the run instead of repeating on a fixed beat.
The other half of the converging pair. Two tracks that merge, occlude one another, then separate -- the classic ID-swap trap for a nearest-neighbour data association.
Crosses SAR_Track_RubbleBypass twice per lap. The bypass is what the robot takes once the main route is blocked, so it meets this one while already mid-replan.
Front bearer of a two-person stretcher party. Both bearers and the stretcher share one key list, so they hold formation rather than drifting apart over a four-minute run.
Rear bearer. Two people plus the load between them read as one long obstacle to a clustering front-end and as three separate tracks to a naive one. That disagreement is the point.
Laps SAR_Building_URB_002 and passes through the 7.5 m canyon on its west leg. Goes fully out of sight behind the block each circuit: track continuation through total occlusion.
Desert track margin. Sparse background and long sightlines -- the easy-detection counterweight to the forest cases.
